subject: the 1 percent rule is dead
preheader: what replaced it, and why it actually matters.
headline: The 1% rule was a heuristic for a different decade.
body: The 1% rule: monthly rent should be at least 1% of purchase price. A $200,000 house should rent for $2,000+. Anything less, skip.

It worked in 2012-2016 because interest rates were 4%, property taxes hadn't doubled yet, and insurance hadn't gone vertical in Florida and Texas. In 2026 the rule is mostly broken. There are basically no metros where a quality property hits 1% — and most of the ones that do are class C with reasons.

What replaced it: actual DSCR and cap rate analysis. A 0.75% rule deal in Nashville with strong appreciation and a DSCR of 1.30 beats a 1.1% rule deal in a depopulating Rust Belt town with DSCR 1.05 and no rent growth. The headline ratio doesn't tell you anything about whether the loan exists or the numbers compound.

The new framework: ignore the 1% rule. Run actual DSCR against today's rates. Look at the 10-year projection with realistic rent growth. Check cash-on-cash against your alternatives. The 1% rule was a shortcut around doing the math. The math is now fast enough that you can just do the math.
TrueCap does all four checks in 60 seconds. The full methodology page walks through exactly which inputs we use and why — worth a read if you want to know what's under the hood.
